questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The destination was never the most important aspect of studying abroad, but UW-Madison had a lot of advantages. It was in an English-speaking country with a somewhat familiar culture, that was still interesting to experience first hand. The city itself, Madison, felt were average for a university city, which allowed me to experience a more representative university experience than in a bigger city. I would also not travel there as a turist, so I would have missed out on it, had I not gone there.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The university has a very informative website for exchange students, though transportation to and from the airport may not be as easy as they claim.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had an exchange student orientation shortly after. I was also part of the Scan Design foundation, which helped me getting my free bus pass, bank account, and student id.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy, but a bit expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's really nice. You can live very close to everything incl. campus without living on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Many places are old and expensive, but good enough.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of paperwork.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Apply special permission for each class incl. discussion section. The method of applying for permission depends on the faculty. This can first be done after the American students have applied for classes, so you also have to make sure, that there is actually room for you. When permission is granted, you can enroll into the class or onto a waitlist.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could write to a service specifically for International Students or the faculty itself. They were quick to answer and usually helpfull.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got some of the classes I originally wanted. Some I didn't get because the process of getting acceptance from both UW-Madison and KU was too slow compared to the deadline, and some I didn't get because there was no more room in the class. I still had good classes though.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for permission from KU as fast as possible. And if the professors at UW don't answer emails then follow up quickly.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were some very good and passionate teachers. There were sadly also many who were unstructured and lazy/unprofessional.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I thought my classes were MA, as KU said they would be. Turns out they were kind of a mix. But the level in general for those courses (and others I've heard about) was far below BA courses at KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The classes were shorter (an hour and 15 min.), they were more focused on class participation, assignments took up a lot of the time, and many classes were more relaxed. Some classes micro managed, in the sense that our grade was affected by how we took notes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Investment Theory, Behavioral Economics, Economics of Health Care, and Population Economics.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Economics of Health Care was really interesting and the professor was passionate and made a great effort. Just be prepared for a big workload.
Population Economics was also really interesting, though the econometrics requirements were quite low for an applied Econ class.

questions.answer: Nothing really comes to mind.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Can't think of anything.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Sports teams seemed to be for students who stayed for more than a semester, but fitness was free and those facilities were extremely good. There were also a lot of clubs, though they weren't for me personally.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports clubs for all sorts, clubs based on identity and activism, you could go to games like ice hockey or basket ball.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can definitely recommend watching a game and going to the Union Terrace while it's still warm.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The same as the exchange students. Also, there is a lot of nature which is great for hikes.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It took some time, but it happened eventually.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just listen to yourself and what feels right.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I sometimes felt that conversations and relations were superficial.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciated the ease with which they invited you to things despite having just met you. This, at least for me, made it way easier to meet new people and experience American traditions.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. There is a lot of school work (not necessarily difficult though) depending on the classes you choose. So consider that before enrolling.
2. Consider joining Scan Design. It has both a scholar ship and a buddy program with activities. Both really helped me during my stay.
3. But if you do travel, Chicago and Milwaukee are relatively close by, which I can recommend.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's really cold in the winter time, so pack a lot of warm clothing and good boots.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part was to experience being a part of a completely different culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Though I really enjoyed being part of the American culture, I still felt more at home in the Danish and sometimes just felt very foreign.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
